notes:
User wants help designing a productive daily routine. Schedule: wakes 7:30 AM, bed 11:30 PM; works 9:00 AM–5:30 PM; one-hour lunch; no fixed evening appointments. Wants one Crash Course episode daily, exercise, and 30 minutes of reading. A proposed routine is exercise 7:45–8:15 AM, Crash Course during lunch (12–1 PM), reading 6–6:30 PM, dinner 6:30–7 PM, free time 7:30–9 PM, and wind-down before bed. Adjustments should account for commute and sleep preparation. User has now completed 50 episodes of Crash Course’s Science series and found it helpful for understanding science basics.

Reading interests: science, history, and self-improvement. Finished *Sapiens*, currently reading *The Power of Habit*, and is interested in *A Short History of Nearly Everything* by Bill Bryson. Plans to buy *Data Science for Dummies* by Lillian Pierson because its beginner-friendly overview, real-world examples, and broad coverage of the data science workflow appeal to them. Previously discussed ML/data-science books including Raschka, Géron, Goodfellow, Chollet, Bishop, and Sutton/Barto.

Currently taking an online Data Science with Python course on Coursera and values practical assignments/projects, reputable instructors, and flexible self-paced learning. Chosen linear-algebra study path: start with Khan Academy’s Linear Algebra course, then Coursera’s Linear Algebra Specialization. Other noted resources include 3Blue1Brown, MIT OpenCourseWare, and Strang.

Learning Spanish with Duolingo. Plans to supplement it with SpanishDict, followed by Coursera’s Spanish for Beginners. Other options mentioned include Coffee Break Spanish, Anki, conversation exchanges, podcasts, and language apps.

Creative skills: watches LinkedIn Learning and wants more Photoshop/Adobe Illustrator resources. Mentioned Udemy, Skillshare, Coursera, Pluralsight, Adobe tutorials, Phlearn, Tutvid, Creative Bloq, YouTube, Behance, and Dribbble; prefers project-based practice and feedback.
